title: 📘 UNIT 2: ANCIENT WORLD CIVILIZATIONS UP TO C. 500 AD
notes: 🌍 Ancient civilizations developed in Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe at different times.

title: 📌 2.1 ANCIENT CIVILIZATIONS OF AFRICA
notes:
🌍 The major ancient African civilizations covered are Ancient Egypt and Nubia.

⭐ Both developed important:
• Political systems
• Economies
• Cultures
• Technologies
• Trade networks

title: 🏺 2.1.1 ANCIENT EGYPT
notes:
📍 Ancient Egyptian civilization began around 3000 BC and flourished in the Nile Valley.

 Upper and Lower Egypt were traditionally unified by Menes around 3200 BC.

💰 Economy → Agriculture was the main economic activity.
 Nile silt renewed soil fertility and supported crops such as wheat and barley.
 Livestock and trade were also important.

👑 Government → Egypt was ruled by an absolute king called the Pharaoh.
 Viziers served as officials, including administrators, tax collectors and judges.
 Pharaohs were regarded as divine rulers.

⛪ Religion → Egyptians were polytheists and worshipped many gods.
 They believed in life after death.

⚰️ Mummification → The preservation of dead bodies was called mummification.
 Developments in mummification contributed to Egyptian knowledge of medicine.

🏗️ Achievements → Major achievements included monumental building technology, writing, medicine and other cultural developments.

🏛️ Major periods → Egyptian history included the Pre-dynastic period, Old Kingdom, Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom.

title: 👑 2.1.2 NUBIA
notes:
📍 Nubia was an important ancient kingdom south of Egypt and was ruled by powerful kings and queens.

💰 Economy → Agriculture, pastoralism and trade were important economic activities.

🤝 Egypt–Nubia relations → The two civilizations influenced one another politically and culturally.

🏗️ Achievements → Nubia was known for building technology and was especially famous for its iron industry.

title: 🌏 2.2 CIVILIZATIONS IN ASIA
notes:
🌍 Major ancient Asian civilizations included Mesopotamia, Persia, India and China.

⭐ Many developed around fertile river valleys and made important contributions to:
• Agriculture
• Government
• Writing
• Science
• Technology
• Religion
• Culture

title: 🏛️ 2.2.1 MESOPOTAMIA
notes:
📍 Mesopotamia was located mainly between the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers, covering areas of present-day Iraq, eastern Syria and southern Turkey.

 The Sumerians developed one of the earliest great river-valley civilizations.

🏙️ Cities → Sumerians built some of the world's earliest cities. 

They used sun-dried mud bricks and constructed large stepped temples called Ziggurats.

🌾 Agriculture → Fertile soil, irrigation and flood control supported large crop production.

👑 Government → Sumerian city-states were ruled by kings who claimed divine authority.

⛪ Religion → Sumerians were polytheists and worshipped many gods.

🛠️ Achievements → Important developments included the plough, potter's wheel, bronze working, mathematics, astronomy, medicine, metalworking and writing.

✍️ Cuneiform → Around 3200 BC, Sumerians developed cuneiform, a complex writing system using ideographic signs.

title: 👑 2.2.2 PERSIA
notes:
📍 Persia covered parts of present-day Iran and Afghanistan.

 The Persians referred to their region as the 'Land of Aryans'.

🏛️ Persian Empire → Cyrus the Great founded the first Persian Empire around 550 BC. 

It became one of the largest empires of the ancient world, extending from the Balkan Peninsula to the Indus Valley and including parts of North Africa.

⭐ Contributions → Persia contributed to government, law, religion, road construction and communication.

📮 Postal service → The Persians developed an organized postal service.

☀️ Religion → Zoroastrianism was the major Persian religion and was associated with the prophet Zoroaster.

title: 🇮🇳 2.2.3 INDIA
notes:
📍 The first Indian civilization developed in the Indus Valley in present-day Pakistan and western India around 2500 BC and reached its peak around 1500 BC.

🧮 Knowledge → People developed systems of counting, measuring, weighing and writing.

🌾 Agriculture → Ditches and canals were used for irrigation.

🤝 Trade → Indian communities traded with one another and with civilizations such as Mesopotamia.

🔨 Technology → Copper and bronze were used to make tools, mirrors, pots and pans. 
Gold was used for ornaments.

👥 Society → Ancient Indian society was organized into social hierarchies based on work and birth.

🕉️ Religion → Hinduism developed from early Indo-Aryan beliefs.
 Buddhism emerged from Hinduism as a reform movement and later spread to Southeast Asia, China and Japan.

title: 🐉 2.2.4 CHINA
notes:
📍 Ancient Chinese civilization developed in the Yellow River region of northern China and later expanded into central and southern China. Major achievements included bronze vessels, war chariots and a writing system.

📚 Zhou Dynasty → The Zhou dynasty overthrew the Shang around 1122 BC and ruled until 256 BC.
 Chinese literary classics and philosophy developed during this period.

🧠 Confucius → Confucius (551–479 BC) was a major Chinese philosopher. 
His teachings formed Confucianism, which emphasized an orderly society and social relationships.

🧱 Great Wall → The Chinese constructed the Great Wall to defend against invaders from Central Asia.

✍️ Writing → Chinese writing was logographic, using pictorial symbols to represent words.

title: 🌎 2.3 ANCIENT CIVILIZATION OF LATIN AMERICA
notes:
🌍 Important ancient civilizations of Latin America included the Maya, Inca and Aztecs.

⭐ They developed advanced systems of:
• Agriculture
• Government
• Architecture
• Mathematics
• Writing
• Engineering
• Religion

title: 🔭 2.3.1 MAYA
notes:
🌎 The Maya were Native American people who developed a major civilization in the western hemisphere before European arrival.
 Their civilization reached its peak around 250–900 AD.

🏛️ Achievements → Architecture, painting, pottery, sculpture, astronomy and mathematics.

📅 Calendar → They developed an accurate yearly calendar.

✍️ Writing → They developed an advanced writing system.

⛪ Religion → The Maya worshipped many gods and goddesses.

🔺 Architecture → They built tall limestone pyramids with small temples on top.

⚔️ Spanish conquest → Spanish domination of the Maya region was completed in the late 17th century.

title: 🛣️ 2.3.2 INCA
notes:
🌎 The Inca were a South American people who ruled one of the largest and richest empires in the Americas.
 Their empire began expanding around 1438.

🗺️ Territory → It included areas of present-day Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina.

🏙️ Capital → Cusco in southern Peru.

🏗️ Engineering → The Inca constructed an extensive road network.

🎨 Crafts → They produced fine objects from gold, silver and other materials.

🧶 Textiles → They produced fine cotton and woolen cloth.

⚔️ Conquest → Spanish forces conquered the Inca Empire after 1532.

title: 🌽 2.3.3 AZTECS
notes:
🌎 The Aztecs were a Native American people who ruled a powerful empire in Mexico during the 15th and 16th centuries.

📍 Center → The civilization developed mainly in the Valley of Mexico.

🏙️ Capital → Tenochtitlan was the largest city and capital.

🌾 Economy → Agriculture was the basis of the economy.

⛪ Religion → The Aztecs worshipped hundreds of gods and goddesses.

✍️ Writing → They used pictographic writing.

⚔️ Conquest → The Aztec Empire was destroyed by the Spaniards in 1521.

title: 🏛️ 2.4 CIVILIZATIONS IN EUROPE
notes:
🌍 The major ancient European civilizations covered are Ancient Greece and Ancient Rome.

⭐ Their major contributions include:
• Political ideas
• Philosophy
• Literature
• Law
• Architecture
• Engineering
• Institutions

title: 🏺 2.4.1 ANCIENT GREEK CIVILIZATION
notes:
🏛️ Ancient Greece emerged about 2500 years ago and became a major foundation of Western civilization.

🏙️ Polis → Greek political life developed around small city-states called poleis.
 A city-state included a city or town and surrounding villages and farmland.

⭐ Major city-states → Athens and Sparta were the best-known city-states.
 They were not united into one nation but shared language, religion and culture.

🏛️ Architecture → The Parthenon, temple of Athena in Athens, is a major example.

🎭 Literature and drama → Greeks developed drama and theatre.

🗿 Sculpture → Greek artists created statues of gods and heroes using marble and bronze.

📜 History → Herodotus and Thucydides were major Greek historians. Herodotus wrote about the Persian Wars, while Thucydides wrote about the Peloponnesian War.

🩺 Medicine → Hippocrates contributed to the development of medicine by identifying symptoms, classifying diseases and suggesting treatments.

🧠 Philosophy → Plato and Aristotle were major Greek philosophers.

🏅 Other influences → Democracy, psychology, Olympic and marathon are terms or ideas associated with Greek civilization.

title: 🏛️ 2.4.2 ANCIENT ROMAN CIVILIZATION
notes:
📍 Roman civilization began in present-day Italy around 753 BC near the River Tiber and became a major force in Western civilization.

⚖️ Law → Roman law influenced the legal systems of many countries in Western Europe and Latin America.

🏗️ Engineering → Romans built roads, bridges and aqueducts. They also constructed public baths and amphitheatres.

🏟️ Coliseum → The Coliseum was Rome's famous amphitheatre.

👑 Early Rome → A series of kings ruled Rome during its early period.

🏛️ Roman Republic → Established in 509 BC after Roman nobles overthrew the king. Two elected officials called Consuls headed the government for one year each. The Senate was the most powerful body and senators served for life.

⚔️ Expansion → Rome expanded through wars, including the Punic Wars against Carthage from 264–146 BC. Roman territory eventually spread around the Mediterranean and beyond.

🏛️ Roman Empire → The Republic ended in 27 BC after civil conflict, followed by the Roman Empire. The Empire lasted until Rome fell in 476 AD.

📚 Roman legacy → Latin language, Latin literature, Roman law and the Julian calendar were important Roman contributions. The Julian calendar became the basis of the modern Gregorian calendar.

title: ✝️ 2.5 RISE AND SPREAD OF CHRISTIANITY
notes:
✝️ Christianity began in Palestine during the first century AD and was based on the teachings of Jesus Christ. Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea under Roman rule.

⚔️ Persecution → Roman authorities regarded Christianity as a threat to imperial unity and persecuted Christians, especially during the reign of Nero (AD 54–68).

👑 Constantine → Emperor Constantine became a Christian in 312 AD. He supported Christianity and helped it spread rapidly.

📜 Edict of Milan → In 313 AD, Constantine ordered religious toleration, giving Christians freedom from persecution.

🏛️ Official religion → Under Emperor Theodosius the Great, Christianity became the official religion of the Roman Empire in 392 AD.

🌍 Spread → Christianity became an important unifying force in Western Europe during the Middle Ages.

⛪ Church division → Disagreements over religious authority, language and rituals eventually contributed to the division of Christianity. In 1054, the Christian Church split into the Roman Catholic Church centered in Rome and the Eastern Orthodox Church centered in Constantinople.

🔔 Reformation → In 1517, the Reformation movement began and Western Christianity was divided between Roman Catholicism and Protestantism.
